note: The protocol conformance cases every SDK must pass (model/PROTOCOL.md section 11). Each harness names a test after the case id, in square brackets, for example `[retry.429-retry-after] …`; scripts/check-conformance.mjs fails a language that skips or fails one. The example cases (cases/examples.json) are checked the same way, as `[example] <id>`.

cases.title: A 429 with Retry-After 2 waits at least 2 s, then succeeds
A 503 with Retry-After 1 waits at least 1 s, then succeeds
A long Retry-After (7 s) is honoured in full
With a budget of 10, two retries on 503 spend it; the next call's 503 fails at once with one request; a failure with no response costs 10
With a budget of 5, a call that succeeds after one retry refunds it, so the next call can retry too
With an empty budget (size 0) the first attempt still goes: a 200 succeeds, and a 503 fails with one request
The idempotency key is generated once and kept across retries
An operation that is not retry-safe (SendMessage) is sent once on a 503
A Retry-After above maxRetryDelay fails at once with the typed error
A list runs to the last page, following nextCursor
Typed events, keep-alive comments ignored, finalMessage() returns the final event's member
A dropped stream resumes with Last-Event-ID, without duplicates
A clean end of stream before the final event also resumes
A stream with a final event, resumed after its answer finished, yields stream.reset and ends: no error, no further reconnect, and finalMessage() fails with NO_FINAL_EVENT
A watch the server ends cleanly reconnects with Last-Event-ID, without duplicates, as often as each reconnect carries events
A watch reconnects with its whole request, what it listens to included, and Last-Event-ID
stream.reset on a conversation watch is delivered as an event with its cursor as its id, and the watch carries on
Each reconnect in a row waits a longer, jittered pause (0.25-0.5 s, 0.5-1 s, 1-2 s), and the fourth fails with STREAM_LOST
A reconnect before any event has arrived sends no Last-Event-ID, and a watch keeps its after cursor
A watch's reconnect sends Last-Event-ID in place of the after cursor it started from
A connection that stayed open at least a minute before it ended starts the reconnect count again: a quiet watch reconnects as often as the server ends it, without STREAM_LOST
Three reconnects in a row whose connections each stayed open under a minute, with no new event, still end in STREAM_LOST
A replayed duplicate is not a new event: reconnects that bring only duplicates still end in STREAM_LOST
On a watch, message.failed is delivered as an event and the watch carries on to the next answer
A stream exposes its request id, and every event its SSE event name
On a stream with a final event, message.failed raises the typed error for its status and ends the stream
A resumed answer ends at its final event, and closes the connection, although WatchConversation stays open after it
stream.reset is delivered as an event with its cursor as its id, the stream carries on after it, and nothing is retried
An unknown event name is skipped
An unknown enum value is kept, not raised

An error code this SDK does not know is kept: on a response, the class is its HTTP status's (a 409 is ConflictError) with the code as sent; on a failed job, the generic error, status 0, with the code as sent
Unknown fields are kept in raw on the output
Unknown fields are kept in raw on nested structures and list items
A 404 is the NotFoundError class with status, code and requestId, with and without X-Amzn-Errortype
A 409 is the ConflictError class
Deleting a document version by number before its versions are numbered is the ConflictError class with code VERSIONS_NOT_NUMBERED, not retried, and nothing is deleted
A 412 on a stale ETag is the PreconditionFailedError class

A 200 whose body is not JSON, for an operation that returns a thing, raises DECODE_FAILED: the generic error, status 0, with the parse failure as its cause (TypeScript cause, Python __cause__, Go Unwrap, Rust source)
wait() on a job that ended failed with no error code raises JOB_FAILED: the generic error, status 0
A file that cannot be read (a path to nothing, or a stream that fails as it is read) raises FILE_UNREADABLE (status 0) with the native error as its cause, and nothing is sent
A sync whose batch awaits a file the call has none for raises INGESTION_ITEM_HAS_NO_FILE (status 0), and nothing is uploaded
A 429 after retries are exhausted carries retryAfterSeconds
A 409 carries retryAfterSeconds from its Retry-After, and is not retried: CreateDocument and a rename onto a path a started batch has reserved for a new document (TARGET_IN_USE)
An HTML 404 with no Caitlyn-Request-Id is the NotFoundError class, with status 404, code HTTP_404, no request id and the body kept as text
A 405 with an empty body is the generic error, with status 405, code HTTP_405 and no request id
A text/plain 502 is the generic error, with status 502, code HTTP_502 and the body text, sent once
An HTTP 409 whose problem body says status 400 is the ConflictError class (not ValidationError), with status 409
A 400 VALIDATION_FAILED for a field both set and cleared carries the field errors
A status the operation does not list (a 404 from CreateUpload) is still that status's class; a status no error shape has (405) is the generic error, named CaitlynError
A 404 with a 20 KiB text/html body keeps exactly its first 8 KiB, truncated; a cut never splits a character; a problem body under 8 KiB is kept whole, not truncated
A connection closed before any response, and a refused connection, are the connection error: status 0, code CONNECTION_ERROR, the cause kept
Cancelling a stream closes the connection and raises the language's cancellation error
Cancelling a single call stops it
If-Match is sent from the call option and the new ETag comes back
clear sends only the clear list, and the field is cleared
Exactly the SDK headers: Caitlyn user agent, Caitlyn-Sdk-Model, no AWS headers
Hostile AWS_* variables and ~/.aws files change nothing
An operation newer than the server's Caitlyn-Api-Version fails before anything is sent
Caitlyn-Request-Id and Caitlyn-Api-Version are on successful outputs

get, update, create, wait() and every other call that gives a thing return that thing's own type (KnowledgeBase, Document, IngestionBatch, Agent, AgentVersion and the rest), its fields at the top level with no wrapper member; a list's items and a watch snapshot's entries are the same types; calls whose output is not a thing keep their named results

A thing from one response (get, update, create, wait()) carries that response's metadata, HTTP status and request id (TypeScript $metadata, not enumerable; Python response_metadata; Go ResponseMetadata(); Rust response_metadata()); a list item and a snapshot entry carry none; the metadata is never serialised with the thing
etag is a field on the thing from every source (a read, a list item, a snapshot entry); when a single read's body has no etag, the SDK fills it from the ETag header
A thing keeps the JSON it was read from as raw, unknown fields included, as every structure does
A list item's etag, given as ifMatch to that thing's update, is accepted: it is the same ETag a read of the thing gives
A successful call's response metadata gives its HTTP status (200), its request id and, where the language keeps it there, its ETag

caitlyn.call, caitlyn.attempt and caitlyn.upload spans with the shared attributes; a failed call and each failed attempt have a status message, error.type, caitlyn.error.code and an exception event; url.full has no query
One span per call, one child span per attempt, traceparent sent
A workspace hostname resolves to https://<workspace>/api

A workspace given as https://<host>, with or without a trailing slash or in capitals, is the bare hostname; a path, a query string, a fragment, user information or a scheme other than https is refused when the client is created, naming the expected form
A workspace given as a hostname or URL sets the token audience https://<workspace>/api; an endpoint override moves the token request, not the audience
A personal access token is sent as the bearer token, with no token request
One token request serves concurrent calls, with the workspace resource and the scopes
A wrong client secret is a sign-in error with the OAuth code and status
A token is replaced before it expires: a minute early, or halfway through a short life
After a 401 the client signs in again once, and the call succeeds
A second 401 after signing in again is raised, with no third attempt
A refused personal access token fails with 401, without retrying
Authorisation code with PKCE (S256), the workspace resource and the scopes, then calls with the saved token
A callback whose state does not match is refused before any token request
An expired access token is refreshed once with the stored refresh token, and the rotated one saved
A stored access token the server refuses is not sent again: the refresh token replaces it
Five calls sent with a token the server then refuses, whose 401s arrive one after another, cause exactly one refresh, and all succeed
Two clients sharing a token store that offers a lock, each calling with an expired access token, cause exactly one refresh: the second uses the tokens the first saved
A refused refresh token clears the token store and fails with invalid_grant
A call before sign-in fails with sign_in_required and sends nothing
A signed STS GetWebIdentityToken call for the workspace audience, one token exchange, then bearer calls
AWS credentials can come from a provider the caller passes, asked when signing in
Without credentials, awsIam uses AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY and AWS_REGION
An STS refusal is a sign-in error with the STS code, and nothing is sent
With no AWS credentials anywhere, awsIam fails with aws_identity_failed and sends nothing
A workload identity token is exchanged once; a token for another workspace is refused
A replayed workload identity token is refused
Session mode sends the cookie, Origin on writes, and no Authorization header
Making a scope, at any depth, sends no request

A scope's call fills its identifiers from the scope (kb.documents(id).get() sends the knowledge base's and the document's), and a folder scope's path is sent without its first and last / in a request path

A named scope sends its fixed value (agent.live.get() reads version live; agent.draft.get() version draft), merges a singleton of the same name (agent.draft.update() is UpdateDraftVersion), and lacks the operations it leaves out (no agent.live.publish or delete)

An operation with @fromScope called on that scope sends the member filled from the scope's identifier: kb.folders('/hr/').access.get() sends folder, kb.documents(id).access.set() sends document, and kb.access.get() sends neither

create returns the new thing's scope, carrying the response's fields and its identifier (agents.create gives agent.draft at once; kb.documents.create gives the document's scope; kb.folders.create the folder's)

The building blocks are under core and take their identifiers as leading arguments: core.uploads.reserve, core.uploads(id).get(), core.ingestion.addItems(kbId, batchId, items), core.operations(kbId, operationId).get()

An estimate sits beside its job: kb.fields.fillIn.estimate(keys) sends EstimateFillInFields; a file job's estimate (kb.documents.create.estimate(file, options)) takes the file plus the estimate's own input members only, sends the file's description and uploads nothing
access.set({readers}) accepts 'inherit', 'public', 'everyone' or {roles, people}, and sends the modelled {kind, …} shape
access.set({readers: 'public'}) sends {kind: 'public'}, and the access read back has kind public, the readers kind's named value in each SDK
access.set() with no ifMatch sends PutAccess with no If-Match header and no read before it; given ifMatch, it sends that value as If-Match, and a stale one fails with 412 PRECONDITION_FAILED

batch.start() with no ifMatch sends StartIngestionBatch with no If-Match header and no read before it, and the batch starts as it stands; given ifMatch, it sends that value as If-Match, and a stale one fails with 412 PRECONDITION_FAILED

On every operation the model marks @ifMatchOptional, the SDK's ifMatch is optional (the type or signature allows leaving it out) and a call without it sends no If-Match header; on every other operation with an If-Match header, ifMatch is required (a type error, or an error raised before anything is sent, where the language cannot express it in the type)
watch() opens the knowledge base's watch with the scope's identifier as its filter, yields the snapshot first, then each change
After a dropped connection, watch() reconnects with no cursor and yields the new connection's snapshot first again

A watch whose connections bring only their snapshot ends in STREAM_LOST after three reconnects: a snapshot is not a new event, whatever its id; an event after it is, and three such reconnects followed by a connection that stays open carry on
wait() returns what the thing's get() returns (a folder, which has no get, its summary from the watch's snapshot), once the snapshot or a later event shows no job running on it

wait() finds the thing in the watch's snapshot under the scope's filter name: a batch under batch, a document under document, a folder under folder (a knowledge base's own wait under knowledgeBase), and returns it as that thing's type; for each of the three, a snapshot that already shows it done ends the wait with that entry
wait() returns on a job that ended completed_with_failures, with the partial failures on the thing
wait() raises a job that ended failed as the typed error for its code, and one that ended cancelled as CANCELLED (an error the SDK raises itself, status 0)
wait() after a delete returns when the thing is gone; on any other call, a 404 ends the wait with the 404

A document (or folder) still being processed can be deleted: the delete is accepted, its processing stops, and doc.delete().wait() ends on the gone rule; the job the delete stopped, which ends cancelled, is part of the delete and does not raise CANCELLED, and the document never comes back

The wait() of a call that cancels (batch.cancel(), doc.cancelProcessing()) returns the thing once its work has stopped (the IngestionBatch cancelled, the Document as it then stands): the job the call cancelled ends cancelled as the call intended and does not raise CANCELLED; every other wait still raises CANCELLED for a job that ends cancelled

A call that starts work returns a handle whose result is the call's response (.result, or the language's equivalent; TypeScript: awaiting it alone), with wait() and watch() that follow that work (TypeScript: one await of create(...).wait(); Rust: the request's own .wait() and .watch(), or send() then wait())

wait() treats a thing as busy while a job on it runs or its status is a working value, even with no job listed: a knowledge base creating, moving or deleting; a document pending, processing or deleting (doc.delete().wait() waits through deleting, then ends on the gone rule); an ingestion batch planning or running; a folder, which has no status, while a folder_change job on it runs

wait() given a time limit that passes raises an error with the code WAIT_TIMEOUT (status 0), as the language's own timeout type (TypeScript and Python a TimeoutError, Go an *Error for which errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded) holds, Rust Error::Timeout), and closes the watch
batch.planned() waits until the batch is planned or past it

A batch's wait() and watch() read the batch again once its uploadsExpireAt plus 30 seconds has passed and it is still open, and carry on from what the read returns: with the batch's ending never sent on its watch, wait() returns the batch completed_with_failures with its unuploaded items failed UPLOAD_EXPIRED, and watch() yields each read as a snapshot; a deadline is read again once, and the timer starts again from each snapshot
A 404 when watch() reconnects ends the watch at once, as the thing being gone (wait() then ends by the gone rule), and does not count towards STREAM_LOST

wait() takes a progress callback (TypeScript onProgress, Python on_progress, Go WithProgress(func), Rust .on_progress(|p| ...)) called with the thing's processing: first the snapshot's, if it is being processed, then each progress event's, in order, never twice for one event; a document's is its DocumentProcessing (stage, percent, eta), a batch's or folder's the running job; the callback is not called once wait() has returned or raised

Each event from watch() has one accessor for a thing's processing (TypeScript and Python processing, Go GetProcessing(), Rust processing()) that reads the snapshot and progress events alike: for a scope's watch, the watched thing's; for the knowledge base's own watch, the thing named by the identifier it is given; nothing when the event carries none

Watch events are read as the model's types, as a call's output is: a snapshot entry's and a change event's timestamps (updatedAt, createdAt) are the language's date type (TypeScript Date, Python datetime, Go time.Time, Rust its date-time type), not strings, so a folder's wait() and ListFolders give the same Folder

Leaving a watch after its first event (TypeScript break out of for await, Python break or leaving its context, Go cancelling the context or stopping the iterator, Rust dropping the stream) closes its connection: the server sees the client disconnect within a second, with no further request
conversation.send(message) sends the message when it is called, whether or not its stream is read
A conversation's send() stream has text(), which yields only the answer's text deltas, in order, and ends at the answer's end

Breaking out of a send() stream's events or text leaves its connection open: finalMessage() (Python final_message(), Go FinalMessage(), Rust final_message()) then drains it, returns the completed message and closes it; a stream left after a break closes when the caller closes it (TypeScript stream.close() or its abort signal, Python leaving its context or close(), Go Close() or cancelling the context, Rust dropping it), and the server sees the client disconnect within a second

send(text, attachments) takes 1 to 10 entries, each a file (any section 14 source) or an existing upload id: it reserves each file with CreateUpload and purpose {conversationId} set to the conversation, sends its bytes, then sends one message whose attachments name every upload in the order given (an upload id passed through as it is); if any file fails to upload, no message is sent and the call raises that file's error; the SDK does not check maxFiles itself, and sending the same files again uploads them again

kb.documents(id).download() calls GetDocumentDownload and returns its {url, expiresAt}, follows no redirect and sends no request to the address; GetDocumentContent, the 302, is the building block core.documents.content

core.documents.content() treats the 302 as its success and returns the address in its Location, unfollowed, sending nothing to it; no SDK's HTTP client follows a redirect (Go stops CheckRedirect, Rust builds its client with redirects off, Python sets follow_redirects off, TypeScript fetches with redirect: manual). In a browser page, where fetch sees only an opaque redirect, it raises REDIRECT_UNREADABLE (status 0, never retried, one request sent) with a message pointing to kb.documents(id).download()
A path, bytes, a one-shot stream and (in a page) a Blob of the same content reserve the same upload: the same name, size, content type and standard-base64 SHA-256
The content type comes from the caller when given, otherwise from the extension table (.pdf, .docx, .md), and is application/octet-stream for an unknown extension
A one-shot stream larger than 8 MiB is spooled and sent intact, and nothing is left on disk after the call
A file over 2 GB fails with FILE_TOO_LARGE before any request
A path whose size or modification time changes between hashing and sending fails with FILE_CHANGED, and its bytes are not sent
A presigned PUT answered 503 is retried and then succeeds, with the same headers and bytes

kb.documents.create(file) reserves an upload, PUTs the bytes with exactly requiredHeaders, then calls CreateDocument with uploadId set to the upload's id, and returns the new document's scope; kb.documents(id).replace(file) adds a version the same way
agents.create with a file at avatar.mark.pictureUploadId reserves the upload with purpose {agentAvatar: true} and sends CreateAgent with the upload's id at that path

kb.ingestion.sync of a folder hashes each file, creates the batch, waits until planned, starts it, form-POSTs each awaiting file in the policy's field order with x-amz-checksum-algorithm SHA256 and a standard-base64 checksum to a key with the URL-safe one, completes the uploads, waits until finished and returns a per-item report
More than 10,000 items: CreateIngestionBatch takes the first 10,000 with awaitMoreItems, core.ingestion.addItems the rest, 10,000 a call, the last call with last: true
At most 6 uploads run at once by default
CompleteIngestionBatchUploads names at most 100 items a call

A policy past its renewal margin (5 minutes, or half its life when that is shorter) is renewed before it is used for the next upload, and a 403 saying the policy expired renews it once and sends that file again
An item Complete fails with CHECKSUM_MISMATCH is uploaded and completed again once

Items left unresolved by the policy go to the caller's resolver, whose resolutions (add, new_version, overwrite) are sent; with no resolver the call fails with INGESTION_BATCH_UNRESOLVED and the batch is left planned

confirm is called with the plan, and false cancels the batch and ends the call with the SDK's own CANCELLED error (status 0, the language's ordinary error type, never its cancellation or interrupt type), carrying the report so far
With removeMissing, each document under the folder with no matching file becomes a remove item
onProgress reports checksum, planning, planned, upload (with bytes), queued, processing and the final state, in that order, and onItem each finished item
A plan that ends the batch failed raises the batch's own failure: its code (conflict_policy_fail for a fail rule, planning_failed when planning could not finish) and message; nothing is started

Cancelling during the uploads stops new ones, aborts those in flight and raises the language's cancellation error; items already finished reached onItem; with cancelIngestion, CancelIngestionBatch is called with ingestion stop
batch.upload.estimate() on a planned batch sends one EstimateIngestion with exactly the items needing bytes (add, new_version, overwrite; not skip, remove, move or update)
Without files, each document is {name, contentType, byteSize} from its batch item

With files, each document is {name, contentType, byteSize} from its matched file plus exactly the hints the caller gave with it (none when none were given), by the rule of estimate.caller-hints; no SHA-256 is computed and no content read beyond size; a file matching no priced item is left out
A draft batch raises INGESTION_BATCH_NOT_PLANNED (status 0, never retried), with nothing sent
A planning batch is waited on until planned, then priced
A batch with no item needing bytes returns an empty estimate, and no EstimateIngestion is sent
More than 10,000 items needing bytes are priced as sync.estimate-many defines
batch.upload() on a batch not started raises INGESTION_BATCH_NOT_STARTED (status 0, never retried), with nothing sent; a when-planned batch is followed until running, then uploaded

While any upload is in flight, the upload policy is renewed on a timer once it is past its renewal margin (at most once a second), so a long final upload outlives the batch's uploadsExpireAt it started under and its item is accepted; no renewal is sent after the call returns, or after it is cancelled
A policy whose renewal margin comes round every half second is renewed on the keep-alive timer at most once a second while the upload is in flight, and the item is accepted

uploadWindowSeconds (on sync) and expiresInSeconds (on reserve) pass straight through; a policy with a short life is renewed once half of it has passed, not at once and then once a second, and the item is accepted
Only awaiting_upload items that have a file are sent: at most 6 at once, the policy's form fields in order, and CompleteIngestionBatchUploads in groups of at most 100
An item with no file stays awaiting_upload, is listed in notGiven, is not reported to Complete and does not reach onItem
A given path that matches no awaiting item is listed in unmatched and nothing is sent for it; a key without its leading / matches
A file of the wrong size is FILE_CHANGED before sending, and storage refusing its checksum is FILE_CHANGED with no retry; neither stops the other uploads
An upload that fails after its retries is UPLOAD_FAILED for that item only: it reaches onItem and items, and is not reported to Complete

The upload policy is renewed once it is past its renewal margin (5 minutes, or half its life when that is shorter), before the next upload, and once after a 403 saying it expired, sending that file again
CHECKSUM_MISMATCH from Complete uploads the item once more; a second mismatch fails it
A second upload() sends only the items still awaiting upload
Awaiting upload() gives {batch, items, notGiven, unmatched} with batch an IngestionBatch; .wait() returns the finished IngestionBatch
Cancelling upload() aborts the uploads, raises the language's cancellation error, and sends no CancelIngestionBatch

An item that ends cancelled (its document was deleted while it was being ingested) is final: onItem reports it once, as cancelled with no failure code, onProgress counts it as done, and it is never uploaded or completed again; a batch whose items ended only indexed, skipped and cancelled (none failed) ends succeeded, and sync() and wait() return it without raising

onItem is called once per item, only when its status is final (indexed, skipped, moved, updated, removed, cancelled or failed), never when its upload is accepted; an upload that still fails after its retries reaches it at once, as failed with UPLOAD_FAILED; when the call is cancelled, onItem has had every item that was final before the cancellation and no other, and is never called after the cancellation error is raised

A cancelled sync's error carries the report so far (TypeScript and Python error.report, Go err.Report, Rust report()): every item, including those accepted but not yet final with their last status, and the batch's counts; onItem only ever had final items. The caller cancelling (an abort signal, a cancelled task, a cancelled context, a dropped future, Ctrl-C) raises the language's own cancellation; a declined confirm raises the SDK's CANCELLED error (status 0) instead; both carry the report

sync() returns its report as batch (the batch as reading it gives it, with its status and counts) and items (every item as listing the batch's items gives it: outcome, resolution, status, document, version and failure), the same two members in every language (TypeScript and Python report.batch and report.items, Go Report.Batch and Report.Items, Rust report.batch and report.items); a cancellation's or a declined confirm's report has the same shape

Pricing more items that need bytes than one EstimateIngestion call takes (10,000 documents) sends them in calls of at most 10,000, in order, and adds the estimates together: documents, pages, mediaSeconds and documentsOfUnknownLength summed, durationSeconds low and high summed, cost low and high summed in its unit and present only when every part has one, details left out; sync.estimate and confirm see the one total

An estimate prices every item that could need its bytes: those resolved add, new_version or overwrite, and those still unresolved whose outcome could take bytes (new, changed or a conflict), as the most the batch could cost; items resolved skip, remove, move or update are not priced. sync's confirm sees that estimate before the resolver runs, and batch.upload.estimate prices the same items

Hints a caller gives a file (TypeScript a description {name, contentType, byteSize, hints} in place of the file; Python UploadFile.from_path, from_bytes and from_stream with hints=; Go caitlyn.WithHints; Rust UploadFile::from_path(...).hints(...) and the other constructors) reach EstimateIngestion as that document's hints, from documents.create.estimate, doc.replace.estimate and ingestion.sync.estimate alike; a file given no hints is described by its name, content type and size alone, with no hints member, and is neither hashed nor read for the estimate. Batch items carry no hints, so nothing is added to them

A call whose response headers do not arrive within the request timeout fails with CONNECTION_ERROR, whose message names the operation and the timeout, after its retries; each timed-out attempt's connection is closed; a watch that only gets keep-alives for longer than the timeout stays open

A storage request that sends and receives nothing for the stall timeout is abandoned, closed and retried; once the retries are spent the item fails with UPLOAD_FAILED, and the detail says storage sent nothing
A large upload that storage reads slowly but steadily, for longer than the stall timeout in all, is not abandoned: its item is accepted

An upload policy with no expiresAt is renewed before each upload starts, every upload is accepted, and no keep-alive timer runs for it; one whose expiresAt is not a time fails the upload with DECODE_FAILED, never a silent loss of renewal

A policy whose formFields have their own key (as createPresignedPost makes them) uploads each item with one key, the item's objectKey: the SDK leaves out the policy's copy of any field it sends itself, and the mock refuses a repeated field
A sync with no confirm never calls EstimateIngestion, and completes when EstimateIngestion would fail
When EstimateIngestion fails, confirm gets the plan with no estimate and the typed error as estimateError, and the sync goes on when it returns true; sync.estimate raises the error
If-Match: * is sent exactly as given when the caller passes it, and matches any version; no helper sends it on its own (the mock refuses an unasked * in every other case)

Each item an upload helper sends has a caitlyn.batch.item span with the batch's and item's ids and the item's path, and the events opened, checked, sending, sent and completed (or failed, with caitlyn.error.code), in that order
